title: Who Prayed Where, 1517–1789: Correcting the Religion Map
note: This audit corrects 31 errors in the religion map for 1517–1789, most visibly an Orthodox Anatolia that was Sunni. It shows how Ottoman rule kept Christian majorities under a Muslim state.

title: Moscow Gets a Patriarch and Calls Itself the Third Rome
note: Constantinople's patriarch installs Job as Moscow's first patriarch in a charter that calls Russia the Third Rome; in 2018 the two churches break communion over Kyiv.

title: How a Jewish Sect Became Rome's Religion
note: Of how the empire that crucified a Galilean preacher ended, 350 years later, by making his church its only lawful faith.

title: Rise of Islam, 610–750
note: Of how a prophet's community in Arabia became a state, defeated two empires, and fought itself over who should rule.

title: The Reformation and Its Wars
note: Of how a friar's protest became a princes' settlement, and why it took 131 years and a continental war to finish.

title: How Buddhism Spread
note: Of how a wandering teacher's order crossed Asia by winning kings and merchants, and why it grew rich enough for an emperor to seize.

title: Qin's First Emperor Orders the Books Burned
note: On Li Si's advice the First Emperor orders private copies of the Odes, the Documents and rival histories burned; historians now doubt parts of Sima Qian's account.

title: Crusaders Sack Béziers and the Cathar War Begins
note: Innocent III's crusade against the Cathars storms Béziers and kills Catholics and heretics alike; the legate claimed almost 20,000 dead, historians count far fewer.

title: Mehmed II Makes the Anti-Union Monk Gennadios Patriarch
note: Mehmed II installs the leading foe of union with Rome as patriarch and hands him the staff himself; later accounts made it the start of a millet system, which historians doubt.

title: The Council of Chalcedon Defines Christ's Two Natures and Splits the Eastern Churches
note: The Oriental Orthodox churches, who call their teaching miaphysite, rejected the council; modern dialogues since 1973 have narrowed the Christological gap.

title: Turkey Turns Hagia Sophia Back into a Mosque
note: On 10 July 2020 a Turkish court voided the museum status and the presidency ordered Hagia Sophia reopened as a mosque.

title: Al-Ghazali Completes The Incoherence of the Philosophers
note: In January 1095 al-Ghazali finished The Incoherence of the Philosophers in Baghdad, branding three Avicennan theses as unbelief.
